title: Crosswind Council
logline: At council, keys may be filed smaller, never grown in secret. No key yet covers the egg.
epigraph: Benefit without cost is rumor; cost without benefit is ruin.
description: Chapter 4 of Lore.Land: Crosswind Council. Boon and bane sit under shared weather with keys that can only be narrowed. The egg rests between them, a self-governing cell no key covers.

content.text: Council Hill kept a great slab of split pine that refused to pick a side. Boof slipped beneath the trestle and set her chin upon the timber between two keys, stumbling, almost, upon the

children.text: —an upright pane of polished weather that returned not a face or a coat of fur, but the exact legal perimeter of what you were permitted to touch. One key was black iron, its teeth notched and filed smaller by generations of honest compromises. The other was gleaming brass, polished smooth, whose keeper constantly leaned over it with a jeweler's rasp, hoping to secretly solder on a wider ward.

content.text: The law of the crosswind was older than the shouting delegates above: a key may be filed smaller in the open. A key may never be grown in secret.

content.text: The Fool’s Mirror shimmered with the fury of the split sky. It whispered in a tone like wind through eaves: "What you see is not what is, but what you are still allowed to do." The delegate of Boon looked into the pane and saw a limitless harvest ready to be seized. The delegate of Bane looked in and saw an unyielding wall of constraints. The egg resting between them saw neither. It was a cell that kept its own internal law, needing no key because no lock on the hill could claim jurisdiction over its shell.

content.text: File a key smaller. Never let brass grow teeth in the dark.
One-footed on the unposted ledger, a tiny iron file tucked behind his ear, he grinned into the split sky.

img.alt: A council table under storm-light, two keys and a coal-dark cracked egg the keys cannot cover.

sections.figcaption: Crosswind Council: keys narrow; they do not secretly widen.

content.text: Boof watched the delegates argue across the pine grain. Boon and Bane sat under one shared roof of clouds and bargained without having to declare war. The table itself was the living membrane between them: a sturdy boundary where opposing factions could share a single turn without either party having to surrender the keys to their house.

Yet neither the filed iron nor the ambitious brass could turn the lock on the egg. The egg was not an asset up for auction, and it was not a tax to be levied. Filing the council's keys smaller only made the self-sufficient warmth of the uncovered shell more luminous against the dark wood.

content.text: Boof left both keys on the table where they lay. A key you do not pick up is a key no clerk can ever accuse you of tampering with. She tucked the feed-sack sling securely against her chest and turned down the southern slope.

Downslope in the valley, the counting rooms had already begun to disagree with themselves—two conflicting receipts that could not both post to the same ledger without splitting the parchment in half. That was not an argument for council debate; that was an unhealed rift in the stone.

loreItems.description: A key may be filed smaller, never grown in secret. That is the council's oldest weather.
The egg is a cell: it keeps its own law. No key on the table covers it.
Sharing across a membrane is not giving the house away. Boon and bane can sit one turn without becoming one office.
